machine: Apple M4 Pro, 12 logical cores, macOS 26.6.1, CPython 3.14.6
contention: OTHER AGENTS WERE RUNNING THROUGHOUT. 3-5 sibling python processes at ~80-100% CPU were visible in ps during every measurement. All wall-clock numbers here are contention-suspect; CPU numbers come from resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) and sample-stack FRACTIONS, which are contention-robust. Where the same slice was run twice the second (more contended) run cost 9% more CPU, which bounds the residual contention error.

A_build_tables_default.what: table.build_tables(spec, features_for_config('default'), trace_store=None, share=None) — one configuration's decision-table fixpoint, in-process, no persisted memo, no artifact written
A_build_tables_default.process_teardown_s: ~2.7 (87.82 s process real vs 83.07 s of measured work + 0.1 s spec load + ~0.3 s import, /usr/bin/time -l on the sampled rerun)

B_conform_sweep_default.what: conform._conformance_config for the default config at horizon 4, against the prebuilt M1.otf and its serialized window enumeration; the unbounded witness top-up hunt is neutered by stubbing _candidate_witness_tokens / _window_witness_candidates to return nothing, so the slice is exactly 'the length-1..L sweep plus the coverage bookkeeping'

marginal_length4_only.note: differencing L4 minus L3 removes the fixed cost (the lazily built _ProspectLiveness probe pile and the 682,842-row coverage bookkeeping) and leaves exactly what one more sweep length costs. This is the figure that governs a horizon-5 sweep, because 2,000,718 of its 2,111,868 texts are length 5.

C_oracle_default.what: conform.oracle_config_worker for the default config against a freshly filtered current-alphabet subset table (111,150 rows) and the prebuilt M1.otf
C_oracle_default.caveat: the ledger and alias files are calibrated against the July artifacts while this subset was filtered from the current 18-token alphabet, so divergent_rows (84,008) is far higher than a clean run's. That inflates the divergence-classification and audit-line work, not the shaping, so 5.67% is if anything a slight UNDERestimate of harfbuzz's share of a clean oracle pass.

method_A_native_sampler.convention: leaf (top-of-stack) frames. _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault = python_bytecode. Any other frame in the CPython binary, plus libdyld _tlv_get_addr (CPython's thread-state TLS lookup) and libsystem_platform memcpy/memset that the object model drives = interpreter_overhead. Third-party/stdlib C extension .so = native_extension. libsystem_kernel = io_or_wait.

build_tables_default.native_libraries_anywhere_in_call_graph: NONE. The only non-CPython binaries appearing at all are libdyld (235 frames), libsystem_platform (59), libsystem_malloc (8), libsystem_pthread (1). Zero harfbuzz, zero zlib, zero hashlib, zero _json, zero _pickle, zero _sre.

conform_sweep_L4_window_over_lengths_1_3.note: this 30 s window landed inside the length<=3 portion of the run, which does only 8,478 of the run's 172,334 shapes. Unrepresentative of a real horizon-5 sweep; kept for completeness.

method_B_cProfile.distortion_direction: cProfile charges roughly a microsecond per CALL EVENT. This workload is almost nothing but call events (9.2 M Engine.candidates calls alone), so the profiled run inflates uniformly across both the Python-frame and the builtin-C bucket; what it does NOT inflate is time the eval loop spends BETWEEN calls (inline arithmetic, attribute loads, tuple building). So cProfile's split understates pure-bytecode work and overstates per-call work. It cannot manufacture a native-library bucket that Method A says is zero, which is the load-bearing agreement.
method_B_cProfile.cross_check_prior_agent_profile: raw/perf/m1-pipeline/build_tables-default.prof (same tree, different session) splits 82.03 / 17.92 / 0.05 / 0.0 — within 0.5 pt of mine.

method_C_python_sampling_thread.tool: raw/perf/attr-m1/sampler.py — a daemon thread reading sys._current_frames()[main] at 200 Hz
method_C_python_sampling_thread.distortion: 84.375 s wall / 83.073 s CPU sampled vs 85.007 / 83.383 unsampled — under 0.4%, i.e. effectively none
method_C_python_sampling_thread.headline: 25.14% of all Python-level leaf samples are in ONE function: the generated frozen-dataclass __init__ (<string>:2). __hash__ adds 5.44% and __eq__ 2.89%. Every model record is @dataclass(frozen=True) WITHOUT slots=True, so each construction pays object.__setattr__ per field through the wrapper-descriptor path, and each hash rebuilds a tuple.
method_C_python_sampling_thread.note: this independently reproduces the m1-pipeline agent's cProfile finding that ~84% of build_tables sits under third_slot_filter's `matters` closure, without cProfile in the room.

multiprocessing_and_serialization.topology: run_m1._spawn_pool builds a `spawn` ProcessPoolExecutor three times (conformance, boundary, oracle) with max_workers=min(jobs, 6). build_tables is deliberately SERIAL so the cross-config TraceShare stays in one process.

measured_pickle_payloads.sent: once per task, 18 tasks per full run
per conform task on the normal path
ONLY on the standalone fallback at run_m1.py:311, and then to all 6 workers

multiprocessing_and_serialization.conclusion: On the path the pipeline normally takes, pickling is 0.13 CPU-seconds out of ~570 — 0.02%. A threaded Rust/Go rewrite would save it, and it is nothing. The one real serialization hazard is run_m1.py:311's `decision=rebuilt[config][0]`, which ships the whole 682,842-row enumeration (21.3 MB, 2.61 s round trip) to every worker — 15.7 CPU-seconds — and it fires exactly when the serialized tables' fingerprint does not match, which is the state this tree is in.
multiprocessing_and_serialization.note_on_read_windows: the worker-side alternative the pipeline prefers is table.read_windows, measured at 1.12 s CPU per config, of which zlib decompression of the 2.58 MB gz (49.5 MB raw) is 0.0195 s. 98.3% of read_windows is Python row parsing, not zlib.

harfbuzz.font: the M1.otf this tree produces — 263 glyphs, a much smaller GSUB than the shipped Senior font

json_plus_gzip_the_trace_memo.note: the calibration agent measured the whole trace-memo write at 17.0 s for the default config. Only ~4.4 s of that is the C json encoder plus zlib; the other ~12.6 s is TraceStore.save's own Python — _rows(), _entry_names(), frozenset().union over rune closures, and the intern-table construction. The memo write is Python-bound, not serialization-bound.

glyph minting + defect gates + emit_gsub.label: CITED from the m1-pipeline agent, not re-measured here

run_oracle x 6 configs.label: DERIVED from 32.24 s MEASURED for one config

weighted_split_whole_pipeline_pct.how: each stage's measured Method-A split weighted by the stage CPU-seconds above; the conform sweep uses the MEASURED marginal harfbuzz share (10.4%, of which ~88% is inside libharfbuzz proper) with the length-4-phase sampler's bytecode:interpreter ratio applied to the remainder; the cold table stage is given 3.0% native for the trace-memo json+gzip it writes (my fixpoint slice, which writes no memo, measured 0.0%).

split_table_stage_only_pct.note: MEASURED directly, no weighting, no derivation. This is the stage the human waits on serially for 195-338 seconds and it contains no native library at all.

table_stage_only.note: there is no native floor here at all, so the ceiling is unbounded and the realistic speedup is whatever the language delivers

python_level_levers_that_need_no_rewrite.frozen_dataclasses_without_slots: MEASURED: 25.14% of Python-level leaf samples are the generated frozen __init__, 5.44% __hash__, 2.89% __eq__ — 36.95% of the sampler's leaf time in generated dataclass methods. Adding slots=True routes attribute stores through a slot descriptor instead of object.__setattr__ + instance dict.
python_level_levers_that_need_no_rewrite.gc: MEASURED: 14.79% of native leaf samples are in the collector (gc_collect_main, visit_reachable, visit_decref, subtype_traverse, tuple_traverse). The working set is 682,842 Transition objects plus a 1.9 M-entry memo, none of it cyclic garbage. gc.freeze() after spec load plus gc.disable() around the fixpoint is close to free.
python_level_levers_that_need_no_rewrite.read_windows: MEASURED: 1.12 s CPU per config, of which zlib is 0.0195 s. 98% Python row parsing.
python_level_levers_that_need_no_rewrite.baseline_subset.filter_table: MEASURED: 3.17 s per table, zlib 0.177 s. 94% Python per-line int(token,16) work over 4,985,767 rows.
